answers.question: Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?
answers.answer: No, skip the Wednesday 16-miler. It is four days before the race, and a run that long adds fatigue you cannot clear by Sunday but adds almost no fitness in that time. Your 20-mile run on Oct 4 and the 12-mile run on Oct 11 already show the endurance you need. Wednesday's marathon-pace work keeps your rhythm sharp instead.

new.analysis:
## What last week shows
Last week was run as planned. Every running day was done at the planned distance, the rest days were kept, and nothing was overrun. The 8-mile quality session included about 4 miles at 8:36/mi, which is marathon pace, so the hard work matched the plan.

Easy runs held at 9:49 to 9:52/mi with heart rate around 139 on every run, the same as three weeks ago. The 12-mile long run came in at 10:00/mi with heart rate 146, and pain stayed at 0 out of 10 all week.

## Why the legs feel flat
Heavy, flat legs are expected in the last week before a taper, after a 20-mile run on Oct 4 and weeks of 40 to 53 miles. The taper exists to clear that load, so the heaviness is more likely fatigue than lost fitness. Your easy pace and heart rate have not moved in three weeks, which is the clearest sign the fitness is still there.

## How this week is built
Running volume drops to about 15 miles before the race, with one short hard session. The marathon-pace reps on Wednesday keep your rhythm sharp, and the short strides keep your legs quick without adding load.

## Race-day pacing
Under 3:45 needs an average of 8:35/mi or faster across 26.2 miles. A slightly slow start protects the last six miles, where the time is won or lost.

| Miles | Pace | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 – 6 | 8:40 – 8:45/mi | Start controlled and let the field settle |
| 7 – 20 | 8:30 – 8:35/mi | Goal pace at a relaxed effort |
| 21 – 26.2 | 8:30 – 8:35/mi | Hold form, and push only if you feel strong |

If the early miles feel easy, let the pace sit at the quick end of the range rather than pushing the start.
